sections.html: Youngstown, the Mahoning County seat, has an estimated 58,832 residents. That's down 2.0% from the 60,049 counted in 2020 and well below the 66,982 counted in 2010. The city grew around coal, iron and steel mills along the Mahoning River, and the effects show in a smaller population than the city was built for and a lot of older housing. The county auditor's office, the courthouse and most of the records you need for a sale are in the city.

Prices here sit at a very different scale than most of Ohio. The 2020 to 2024 median home value is $63,300 and median rent is $728, with 56.2% of the city's 24,982 households owning. Median household income is $34,408.

  • Monthly owner costs run $916 with a mortgage and $379 without.
  • Youngstown State University, with about 11,000 students, is the largest employer in the city.
  • Health care is the biggest economic sector.

At values this low, a repair bill can swallow much of the price. Buyers and investors count every roof and plumbing problem, so know your house's condition before you set an asking price.

Downtown holds government buildings, banks and venues such as the Covelli Centre and Powers Auditorium, with Youngstown State University and the Butler Institute of American Art just to the north. The North Side includes Brier Hill, Crandall Park, North Heights and Wick Park, where industrial executives built mansions that still stand in historic districts. The South Side is the densest part of the city and includes Oak Hill, Erie, Warren and Lower Gibson.

Interstate 680 serves the city directly and connects to I-80, the Ohio Turnpike and State Route 11. State Route 711 runs north, and the Madison Avenue and Himrod Avenue expressways form a freeway loop around downtown. The Youngstown City School District covers almost all of the city.

Registration is the Youngstown rule that surprises sellers most. Under Section 546.11 of the city's Codified Ordinances, every rental property must be registered and hold a city license renewed annually, other than public housing and Section 8 units, which follow federal inspection rules. Except for owner-occupied homes, all properties must now be registered.

  • The fee is $40 for a single rental unit. In a multi-unit building it is $40 for the first unit and $25 for each additional unit.
  • An unlicensed rental can be fined $100 for each week it is unlicensed, and criminal penalties are possible.
  • Once the form and fee arrive, a provisional license is issued for one year while an inspection is scheduled within 30 days.
  • If the property fails inspection the owner has 30 days to fix the violations, and each re-inspection costs $40.
  • Cancelling an inspection after 8:00 a.m. on the day costs $25, and later late cancellations cost $100 each.

Vacant properties have their own registration program run by the same office. Before you list a vacant house, call the Property Registration Department at (330) 742-8743 and ask whether the address is registered and whether fees are open. The office keeps weekday hours from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

sections.h2: A house on the demolition list
sections.html:
Youngstown decides which houses are condemned, so ask the city first. Call the Property Code Enforcement and Demolition office at (330) 742-8888 to find out where an address stands. The Mahoning County Land Bank acts at the request of cities, villages and townships when demolition funds are available.

The Land Bank answers a few questions that come up in sales. It owns no houses for renovation. It holds no owner phone numbers, so a buyer must find the deeded owner through the auditor's property search. And buying a house for $1 is an urban legend.

If a house is torn down, taxes still follow the building for a time. Taxes are collected a year behind, so you're still taxed on the building's value if it was standing on January 1 of the tax year being collected. A demolition permit for a Youngstown residence comes from the city's Property Code Enforcement and Demolition Department.

Ohio requires each county auditor to reappraise every parcel every six years. Mahoning County completed its reappraisal for tax year 2023, with taxes collected in 2024, and the next reappraisal is for tax year 2030. A triennial update, which studies sales without visiting each property, applies to tax year 2026 with taxes collected in 2027.

Owners who think the county's number is high file a Complaint Against the Valuation of Real Property, accepted from January 2 through March 31. Three officers sit on the Board of Revision, the auditor, the treasurer and the commissioners' president, and the hearing covers value only. Its address is 120 Market Street in Youngstown, and the auditor's office can be reached at (330) 740-2010. For payment questions, call the county treasurer at (330) 740-2460.

Evidence the Mahoning Board of Revision accepts for residential value complaints
EvidenceWhat to submit
Recent saleClosing statement, purchase agreement and conveyance statement for a sale within 24 months, with a notarized arm's-length affidavit
ListingA listing agreement if the property is currently for sale
AppraisalA report by a certified appraiser for tax valuation, subject to review
ConditionPhotographs with professional repair estimates
New constructionBuilder-certified costs for work five years old or less

A tax increase by itself isn't a ground for a value complaint, because taxes result from voted levies.

The state disclosure form under Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 covers most one to four unit sales, with carve-outs for foreclosure sales, deeds in lieu, court-ordered transfers and estate fiduciaries. Anyone selling in one of those roles should confirm which carve-out applies.

The city also publishes a Property Transfer Affidavit, among the forms on its code enforcement page. Ask the Property Code Enforcement and Demolition office whether your sale needs one before you set a closing.

sections.h2: When a cash offer makes sense
sections.html:
A cash offer makes sense when the cost of repair, a rental license problem or a vacant-property registration issue would hold up a conventional buyer's financing. A lender's appraiser and inspector will look closely at a house with roof, plumbing or foundation problems, and the low values here leave little cushion.

Compare more than one offer, ask who pays closing costs, and get the closing date in writing. Request the settlement statement early and check that any unpaid city fees or taxes come out of your proceeds.

Begin by finding out how the city sees your address. Call the Property Registration Department about rental or vacant registration, and the Property Code Enforcement and Demolition office about any condemnation or demolition status. Fix or settle open fees so they don't surface at the title search.

Next, handle the county side. Confirm with the treasurer what is owed, and decide whether you want to file a value complaint during the January 2 to March 31 window. If you've lived in the house and are selling as an heir or fiduciary, check which disclosure carve-out applies.

Last, choose how to sell. An as-is buyer may close sooner and skips the appraisal, but registration, taxes and the disclosure rules still apply. Check that city fees and unpaid taxes come out of your proceeds on the settlement statement.

faqs.q: Do I have to register a rental before I sell a Youngstown house?
faqs.a: If the house is rented, it must be registered and hold a city license each year, and an unlicensed rental can be fined $100 for each week. Call the Property Registration Department at (330) 742-8743 to confirm the status of your address before closing.

faqs.q: What if my Youngstown house is vacant and on the demolition list?
faqs.a: Call the Property Code Enforcement and Demolition office at (330) 742-8888. Local governments decide which houses are condemned, and the Mahoning County Land Bank acts on their requests when funding is available.

faqs.q: When do I file a value complaint in Mahoning County?
faqs.a: File between January 2 and March 31. Complaints for tax year 2026 begin January 2, 2027, and mail or in-person filing goes to the Board of Revision at 120 Market Street.

faqs.q: Is there a disclosure exemption for estate sales in Youngstown?
faqs.a: Yes. The disclosure statute excuses an estate fiduciary, and it also excuses transfers made by court order.

faqs.q: Will I still pay tax on a Youngstown house I demolish?
faqs.a: Yes for the year in question. Taxes are collected a year behind, so a building standing on the January 1 tax date is still taxed that year.
